title.en: Practice Sheet: Machine Learning for Everyone

summary.en: Use pictures, paper rules and short explanations to review the first module without programming.
summary.bn: ছবি, কাগজের নিয়ম আর ছোট ব্যাখ্যায় প্রথম মডিউল ঝালিয়ে নাও; প্রোগ্রামিং লাগবে না।

keywords: Practice Sheet: Machine Learning for Everyone

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: An optional plan for a future program

practice.title: Picture evidence
practice.statementHtml: For Pictures 1 and 2, identify p6’s measurements and the card wrongly named by the four-fence.
hints: Read a row, then compare a predicted name with its actual label.
practice.answerHtml: p6 has size six and sweetness seven, with mango as label. At the size-four fence p5, an apple at size five, is incorrectly predicted mango. Its height does not change its side.

practice.title: Feedback match
practice.statementHtml: Match labelled photos, unnamed toy measurements and rewarded maze moves. Include the role of feedback.
hints: Each task provides different teaching help.
practice.answerHtml: Labelled photos provide correct answers for supervised prediction. Unnamed toy measurements support unsupervised structure finding. Maze moves influence later states and rewards, making an action-learning reinforcement setup.

practice.title: A careful fence count
practice.statementHtml: Count errors when the ten-fruit fence is at 3 and then at 5. Explain the difference card by card.
hints: Track p4 and p5 when the line moves.
practice.answerHtml: At three, p4 and p5 are apples predicted mango. Moving to five puts both on the apple side while all mangoes remain right. Counts change from two to zero because those two disagreements disappear.

practice.title: The overfitting story
practice.statementHtml: Write three sentences comparing the flexible and simple models on the six-plus-four demonstration.
hints: Use both training and hidden results.
practice.answerHtml: The flexible rule copies all six training labels and makes zero training mistakes. It misnames the hidden apples near size three, giving two test mistakes. The simple fence misses one training label but none of these four hidden cards, so fitting old details more closely was not better here.

practice.title: Question an app
practice.statementHtml: Write a five-question review for a fictional class-photo app and suggest a less sensitive alternative.
hints: Include correction and permission, not just accuracy.
practice.answerHtml: Ask what the app predicts, whose examples taught it, what permission covers collection and sharing, who experiences wrong guesses and who can correct them. Use invented drawings instead of real faces when that teaches the same lesson.

practice.title: Plan the project
practice.statementHtml: Outline Nana’s paper busy-morning workflow with a baseline, hidden check and monitoring.
hints: Begin with the decision time and end with a fallback.
practice.answerHtml: Define busy and the before-opening decision. Collect consistent invented forecast and school cards, reserving hidden answers. Compare always quiet with a trained rain rule, record hidden predictions before opening labels, then monitor mistakes during a cautious trial with spare baskets and Nana able to override advice.

quiz.prompt: Worksheet Picture 1: what are p6’s two features and its answer label?
options: Size 7, sweetness 6; apple
Size 6, sweetness 7; mango
Card number 6, label 7; size
Size 6, sweetness 7; identifier
quiz.explanation: Read across p6: six and seven locate the dot, while mango supplies the label colour. Its identifier is only a reference.

caption.en: Ten fruit cards and their exact two-feature positions.
caption.bn: দশ ফলের কার্ড আর দুই ফিচারের ঠিক অবস্থান।

quiz.prompt: Worksheet Picture 2: how many mistakes does the size-four fence make?
options: Zero, because every apple is left
Two, on p6 and p10
One, on p5
Five, on every mango
quiz.explanation: The size-five apple p5 lies right of four and receives mango. All other dots match the stated side rule.

caption.en: Predict Apple on or left of size 4; Mango on the right.
caption.bn: আকার 4 বা বাঁয়ে আপেল, ডানে আম অনুমান।

quiz.prompt: Worksheet Picture 3: which setup finds groups in the six unnamed toy dots?
options: Supervised naming from supplied correct groups
A fixed alarm schedule
Reinforcement from the shown reward tokens
Unsupervised learning
quiz.explanation: There are observations but no supplied group names or reward sequence. Seek useful similarities and state the grouping purpose.

caption.en: Six toy measurements without supplied class labels.
caption.bn: দলের লেবেল ছাড়া ছয় খেলনার মাপ।

quiz.prompt: Worksheet Picture 4: which rule has no training errors but two test errors?
options: The flexible nearest-size rule
The simple fence
The flat always-apple rule
No rule in the picture
quiz.explanation: Look for a zero training bar beside a test bar of two. Only the flexible model has that pair in this demonstration.

caption.en: Six training and four hidden cards: counts from three fitted size-only rules.
caption.bn: ছয় ট্রেনিং, চার টেস্ট কার্ডে তিন আকারভিত্তিক নিয়মের ভুল।

quiz.prompt: Worksheet Picture 5: what does the empty late-bus record row tell you?
options: They have been measured as the slowest
Those children lack recorded race opportunities, so their speeds remain unknown
They should be excluded without another chance
All class measurements are complete
quiz.explanation: Zero records measures absence of observation. It cannot supply the missing running times or justify treating them as weak runners.

caption.en: Recorded race opportunities, not running speeds: three early-bus records and no late-bus records.
caption.bn: এটি দৌড়ের সুযোগ, গতি নয়: আগের বাসে তিন রেকর্ড, দেরির বাসে নেই।

quiz.prompt: The paper instruction says apple for size five or less. What names follow for sizes 4, 5 and 6?
options: Apple, mango, mango
Mango, apple, apple
Apple, apple, mango
Mango, mango, apple
quiz.explanation: Four and five satisfy the apple side including equality. Six is larger and receives mango. Read the words before counting.

quiz.prompt: Eight cards are available and three are sealed for checking. How many remain in training?
options: Three
Eight
Eleven
Five
quiz.explanation: Remove the three sealed cards from the eight available. Five are left for learning, and the sealed answers stay outside that step.

quiz.prompt: Which pair correctly matches task and feedback?
options: Naming fruit from labelled cards: known answers
Unnamed toy grouping: a supplied official answer for every toy
Maze action learning: no actions or consequences
Fixed alarm: a trained reward-seeking policy
quiz.explanation: A fruit name label provides supervision. Grouping unnamed toys and learning from action rewards use different help.

quiz.prompt: A robot recites practice-book answers but fails rearranged unfamiliar questions. What should you check next?
options: Only whether it repeats the old sequence faster
Its guesses on different hidden examples, fixed before answers are shown
Whether it can see every exam answer first
Whether its case has a brighter colour
quiz.explanation: A fresh hidden task checks transfer instead of familiarity with the book. Record predictions before revealing answers.

quiz.prompt: Which step belongs before collecting Nana’s morning records?
options: Choose a rule from final test answers
Publish every customer detail
Define the question, label meaning and decision time
Declare the model permanently accurate
quiz.explanation: Clear timing and meaning determine which observations are appropriate. They also prevent later outcomes from being used as earlier clues.

quiz.prompt: Why might six copies of one fruit be weaker evidence than six varied, reliably named fruit?
options: Copies necessarily change every measurement
Different examples remove all need for checking
A smaller pile always guarantees better learning
Copies add little about situations unlike the original
quiz.explanation: Relevant variation can expose limits. The benefit depends on content and quality, not a rule that every larger or smaller pile wins.

quiz.prompt: A video app recommends drawing after earlier viewing. What should you avoid assuming?
options: That the app knows the viewer’s whole personality
That viewing can supply an imperfect clue
That a recommendation might be wrong
That the viewer can choose something else
quiz.explanation: A recorded action is limited evidence of preference. It is not a complete account of someone’s interests or intentions.

quiz.prompt: A class game needs face-like patterns. Which plan best reduces privacy concerns?
options: Post every real face publicly without asking
Use invented drawings instead of classmates’ face photos
Assume a name tag supplies consent
Copy private albums into an unknown service
quiz.explanation: Pretend drawings teach the pattern task without collecting identities. Real identifiable records require an appropriate purpose and permission.

quiz.prompt: After correcting a hidden-test mistake, a group adjusts its model. Which description is honest?
options: The same answers are still completely unseen
The old score proves the revised rule’s future accuracy
The revealed set helped development; a new final check is needed
Deleting the mistake makes the set fresh again
quiz.explanation: Once answers influence a change, that collection is part of development evidence. Reserve new data for an independent final judgement.

quiz.prompt: Who must be able to fix a wrong model-assisted school decision?
options: Only the model, because people have no further role
Nobody if a number was printed
Only classmates guessing private information
A responsible person with a reachable review route and authority
quiz.explanation: Responsibility remains with people operating and choosing the service. Review must lead to possible correction, not just another automatic approval.

quiz.prompt: What does a plausible Bangla next-word completion establish?
options: That the suggested continuation fits a learned text pattern
That Nana definitely intends the suggested plan
That every claim in the sentence was verified
That no other continuation is acceptable
quiz.explanation: Text patterns can guide fluent guesses. Meaningful intention and factual truth need evidence beyond the continuation itself.

keyPoints.en: Count disagreements one card at a time.
Name the feedback before naming the learning setup.
Keep final checking answers outside model choice.
keyPoints.bn: শেষ যাচাইয়ের উত্তর নিয়ম বাছার বাইরে রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Ask who can question a prediction.
keyPoints.bn: কে অনুমান নিয়ে প্রশ্ন করতে পারবে, জিজ্ঞেস করো।

examQuestions.question: Explain learning from examples using Mina’s cat recognition, without assuming a computer has a human mind.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Mina can use earlier pictures to recognise an unfamiliar cat. A computer can use supplied examples to choose a reusable rule for a similar prediction task. That observed ability does not establish feelings or a human understanding of cats.

examQuestions.question: State p6’s example, features and label from Picture 1.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The example is the single fruit p6. Its observed features are size six centimetres and sweetness seven on the invented scale. Its answer label is mango. The card identifier keeps track of the row.

examQuestions.question: Use Picture 2 to count disagreements at fences 3, 4 and 5.
examQuestions.answerHtml: At three, apples p4 and p5 are wrongly on the mango side, making two errors. At four, only p5 disagrees, making one. At five, all ten labels match, making zero.

examQuestions.question: Which cards have size six and how do their two positions differ?
examQuestions.answerHtml: p6 and p10 both lie at horizontal size six. Their sweetness values are seven and nine, so p10 is two vertical units above p6. Both known labels are mango.

examQuestions.question: Match named fruit cards, unnamed toy groups and maze rewards to learning setups, explaining each match.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Named fruits provide answer labels for supervised learning. Unnamed toy grouping seeks structure without supplied answers, so it is unsupervised. Maze action choices lead to states and rewards, matching reinforcement learning.

examQuestions.question: Read Picture 4 and report all six mistake counts with pile sizes.
examQuestions.answerHtml: For six training cards and four test cards, flat has three and two errors. Simple has one and zero. Flexible has zero and two. The different pile sizes matter; the bars report counts rather than percentages.

examQuestions.question: Explain why the flexible model’s perfect training result does not establish the best new-card performance.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Training cards can be memorised. Here the flexible nearest-size rule copies the isolated size-three mango, causing two hidden apples nearby to be misnamed. The simple fence has one training error but no errors on these four hidden cards. This illustrates a limit of training scores, not a universal ban on flexible models.

examQuestions.question: Eight cards include three reserved checks. How many training cards remain, and which labels can choose the rule?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Five cards remain in training. Their known labels may guide rule choice. The three reserved labels stay hidden until predictions are fixed. Opening them first would change their role from untouched checking evidence.

examQuestions.question: Describe a paper program plan for the size-five fruit instruction, keeping a guess separate from learning.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Receive a measured size. Compare it with five, including equality on the apple side. Report apple or mango. If the actual label later becomes available, record whether the guess matched. Do not secretly change the rule while claiming it was the original prediction.

examQuestions.question: Use Picture 5 to explain why absence of a race record is not a low race speed.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The table counts recorded opportunities: three early-bus records and no late-bus records. It supplies no speeds for unrecorded children. Give a suitable chance to be measured and review the selection process instead of inventing poor performance.

examQuestions.question: Suggest privacy and correction safeguards for a classroom photo or message app.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Use drawn faces or invented messages when possible. For needed personal records, explain purpose, access and appropriate permission with responsible adults, collecting no more than necessary. Provide a reachable way to inspect a wrong result, correct it or seek human review.

examQuestions.question: Walk through Nana’s workflow and explain what happens when rainy mornings later become busy.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Define the useful before-opening question and consistent busy label. Collect and clean relevant cards, reserve hidden answers, compare a baseline and train a rule, then assess fixed predictions. During use, record results and retain a fallback. Repeated changed outcomes trigger a review of examples, rule and question rather than a claim that the earlier score still guarantees success.
